kicker: AI data centres are a great lake draining the memory chips from the small wells: phones and laptops.
summary: AI does not live in the cloud — it competes for every memory chip with the phone in your pocket.

quiz.q: Why might the AI boom make phones and laptops dearer?
options: Phone makers must pay licence fees to AI companies
Factories send memory to AI, leaving less for phones
Import taxes on phones have doubled this year alone
New phones need much bigger screens to be able to use AI
quiz.explain: Big AI companies sign multi-year contracts to buy memory for their data centres. Less is left for phones and laptops, so prices rise.

desk.label: AI's writing desk
desk.art: A low black lacquer desk on moss, under a paper lantern hung from a bamboo pole. The desk top is RAM; the chip is the black inkstone in the middle, the scribe kneeling behind it; the scrolls are data. Beside the inkstone stands a tower of ten celadon plates: HBM, the AI chip's own memory. Behind, stepping stones lead into the mist to a white-walled storehouse, the storage drive. The wider the desk, the more scrolls lie open at once and the faster the brush runs.
desk.towerAria: The HBM plate tower by the inkstone: open it layer by layer
desk.closePrompt: Touch again to stack the plates back
desk.slider: Your computer’s RAM (the width of the desk)
desk.small: Cramped desk: data has to go to the storehouse (the drive) and come back
desk.large: Wide desk: all the data within reach
desk.stackLabel: HBM · layers of memory chips stacked right by the AI chip

insights.text: RAM is the model’s desk. On a cramped desk the model keeps putting data away on the drive and fetching it back, so it slows right down.
AI chips have a desk of their own: HBM, layers of memory chips stacked right beside the chip, moving data many times faster than ordinary RAM.

detail.text: For example, an NVIDIA H200 chip has 141 GB of HBM and moves 4.8 terabytes of data a second.
Making HBM takes more factory capacity than ordinary RAM; the next slide shows what follows.

prompts: Drag the board to widen the desk
Drag the board to both ends: the narrowest desk and the widest

Touch the tower again to stack the plates back

wells.label: The lake drinks the wells
wells.art: Looking down from a hilltop: in the dip of the brow stands the stone sluice of the memory-chip factory, one source flowing two ways. Bamboo pipes carry water to three small stone wells carved Phone, Laptop and Graphics card; over the brow, water falls to a great moonlit lake in the valley, its shore carved AI data centres, lined with rows of lit halls. Each pull of the sluice is a long-term contract: the run to the lake grows, the lake rises and lights another row; the runs to the wells shrink and their water sinks deep into the stone.
wells.prompt: Pull the sluice up: a new contract
wells.gateAria: The Long-term contract sluice: pull it up, or press it, to sign another contract

facts.text: Oct 2025: SK hynix, one of the three biggest memory-chip makers, said all of its 2026 output already has buyers.
The big cloud companies reserve memory with long-term contracts, some for five years or more.

insight.text: Memory-chip factories send their output to AI data centres first, so what flows to phones and laptops runs dry.

bill.label: Who gets the bill
bill.art: An accordion ledger runs straight from the great lake under the moon (the data centres) toward the viewer, over raked sand, to the phone stall at the garden gate. On the counter, a phone hangs a price tag and a RAM tag. Drag the stone paperweight along the ledger: each milestone's fold stands up as it passes and a scrap of the bill flies to pin itself on the price tag; the two DRAM-price folds lie on the ground, the second five times the first. At today, the RAM tag shrinks.
prompts: Drag the paperweight along the ledger to the stall
Look at the phone's price tag
bill.sliderAria: Drag the stone paperweight along the ledger through the milestones of the memory squeeze

board.text: Buying a device now: compare the price and the GB of RAM.

milestones.label: Micron stops selling RAM to consumers

fact.text: Micron, one of the three biggest memory-chip makers, stopped selling RAM and SSDs to consumers (its Crucial brand); shipments only ran to the end of Feb 2026.
IDC, a market-research firm, forecasts the average phone price in 2026 at a record 523 USD.

milestones.label: J.P. Morgan: memory chips 5× the price

fact.text: J.P. Morgan estimates DRAM (the memory chips RAM is made of) will cost over 5 times as much at the end of 2026 as at the start of 2024.

horizon.text: IDC: phones under 100 USD may no longer make a profit.

insight.text: As memory gets dearer, the phone at the stall gets dearer too: IDC forecasts a record 2026 average of 523 USD.

detail.text: People call this “chipflation”: inflation driven by chips. Like the power bills at station 18, the AI boom pushes costs onto people who don't even use AI.
IDC also forecasts that phone sales will fall 12.9% in 2026.

refill.label: When will the wells refill?
refill.art: A dry well in the near corner, a great sky above it is the stage. Three stones stand on along the curve of its curb, farther and farther toward the horizon, each bringing its weather: heat shimmer over a clear sky and a cracking curb; masons raising a fab on a far hill under a cloud just forming; rain clouds rolling in, and the moon's reflection in the well at last, still trembling, not yet round.
refill.prompt: Touch each stone round the dry well

view.text: The memory shortage will last for years; markets often underestimate how long new factories take to build.
The company is building another factory (M15X) and raising investment in 2026 to make more memory chips.
Memory prices will settle by mid-2027; the phone market recovers slightly that year, then rebounds in 2028.

common.text: No one sees the well filling up again this year. The question is whether new factories open first, or AI demand cools first.

insight.text: If you need a computer this year, don’t wait for RAM prices to return to what they were: every forecast has them high until at least mid-2027.
